_doc: Verified order of battle: what the Official Records and the printed state volumes say, per unit, with tier, citation ids and the basis of every range. A unit without a non-lead source is unverified; nothing is filled in. Evidence ids resolve in kit/evidence_index.json.

rules.ranges: low is the lowest and high the highest figure of one kind (basis and men) among its documented lines (inferred lines only when no documented line exists); kinds are never mixed
rules.casualty_total: the printed aggregate, else the sum of the three kinds when each is stated, else a statement of all three kinds together (officers and men lost), else null (never a partial sum, never 0); a combined statement of two kinds (killed and wounded) is carried in the figures as combined and makes no aggregate; a basis whose lines give no aggregate has figures and no range
rules.status: verified = roster, commander and strength each verified; partly = some evidence; unverified = none
rules.comparison: proposed for gate Q01: a layer figure passes when it lies inside the range of one kind of its unit; a unit with no verified range is reported unverified (neither pass nor failure). A range with spans_dates true holds figures dated differently (by_as_of gives each date its own low and high): a gate that knows the date of the figure compares it with the by_as_of entry that holds that date, and never passes it on the wide span
rules.strength_by_as_of: by_as_of: each as_of of the lines of one kind with its own low, high and number of lines (undated lines under "undated"); spans_dates is true when there is more than one

value.note: Address of Col. John B. Bachelder at the dedication of the regiment's monument, printed in New York at Gettysburg vol. 2 (pp. 613-616).

Fox, Regimental Losses (1889): the losses it prints (9, 59, 164) are the return's figures, which the inscription of the position marker gives as 11, 62 and 159.

value.note: of the brigade staff; brought the order to withdraw between half-past three and four o'clock; the full name is that of the roster and index of the history and of Colonel Stone's report

value.name: John E. Parsons
value.note: acting assistant adjutant-general of Stone's brigade; the given names are in brackets in the print

value.name: William M. Dalgliesh
value.note: acting aide of Stone's brigade, later acting assistant adjutant-general (the reports of the 149th and 150th are addressed to him); his horse was shot under him

value.name: B. Walters
value.note: acting aide of Stone's brigade, afterwards of Wister and Dana; "especially praised for his gallantry in rallying and leading in repeated charges"
Col. Wister, 13 September 1863 (p. 334). Col. Dana gives 1,315.
Col. Dana, 29 July 1863 (p. 338); his regimental figures 465, 450 and 400 add to 1,315. Col. Wister gives 1,300.

taken_into_action|not_stated.basis: the report says the unit went into action with N; not stated; as of 1863-07-01; 1 line (OR27-1-R063)

taken_into_action|rank_and_file.basis: the report says the unit went into action with N; rank and file; as of 1863-07-01; 1 line

value.name: Charles W. Betzenberger
value.note: List of officers killed in the Return of Casualties (OR27-1-R013 pp. 188-190, heading OFFICERS KILLED), by state and regiment. Musser: wounded in the hand early, fell mortally wounded near the town.

value.name: Lyman E. Nicholson
value.note: List of officers mortally wounded (OR27-1-R013 pp. 191-192, heading OFFICERS MORTALLY WOUNDED): rank and heading read on the scanned page (pdf page 215), where the OCR separates the ranks from the names.

value.name: Reamer
value.note: brigade surgeon of Stone's brigade; no given name is printed

value.name: Scott
value.note: assistant surgeon of the 143rd Pennsylvania; stayed with the wounded of 2 and 3 July; no given name is printed

value.name: C. C. Plotz
value.note: wounded early in the action and again on the road into town

value.name: George N. Reichard
value.note: wounded in the shoulder while holding the road, then taken prisoner

value.name: Asher Gaylord
value.note: wounded in both legs in the peach orchard and left on the field

value.name: William Lafrance
value.note: shot through the arm while passing through the town

value.name: William A. Tubbs
value.note: slightly wounded in the head and taken prisoner

value.name: H. M. Gordon
value.note: shot through the leg and taken prisoner while crawling after the regiment

value.name: O. E. Vaughan
value.note: a slight bruise on the head from a ball, which Musser says may properly be called a wound

value.name: John Jones, jr.
value.note: adjutant; reported himself wounded, the place and gravity unknown to Musser

value.name: C. K. Hughes
value.note: slight wound from a piece of shell; left the field

value.name: C. M. Conyngham
value.note: wounded early in the action; commanded Company A when it was detached as skirmishers (Dana's report); Musser prints Capts. Reichard, Plotz and Conyngham where he lists Plotz as Lieutenant elsewhere

value.name: Lyman R. Nicholson
value.note: wounded through the shoulder after leaving the peach orchard, refused to have anyone stay with him; the list of officers mortally wounded prints Lyman E. Nicholson, 143d Infantry (us-1c:0344)

items.printed: Enfield rifles
items.note: pattern not named

items.printed: sphere of the First Corps, blue for the Third Division
knapsacks and blankets left behind

commanders.name: H. Boyd McKeen
commanders.role: colonel of the 81st Pennsylvania, assigned to the regiment by Colonel Cross

change.detail: informed the company commanders at Uniontown, Maryland, on the evening of 30 June that he had come "by order of Colonel Cross to assume command of it"; he took the brigade when Cross fell on 2 July

McKeen, who became brigade commander when Cross fell, "directed Colonel McFarlane to resume command of the Regiment"; "from that moment until the battle ended the Regiment was in charge of Colonel McFarlane"

value.name: James A. Beaver
value.note: absent from the Gettysburg campaign with the wound received at Chancellorsville (Forster's address, p. 882: "had not recovered from the severe wound"); rejoined on 23 July 1863 near Ashby's Gap

value.name: George A. Fairlamb
value.note: absent wounded in June 1863 (the editor's note to Captain Forster's letter of 23 June); the regiment's major, wounded at Chancellorsville where he commanded after the colonel fell (p. 242)

items.printed: a formidable sword bayonet
items.note: the regiment's bayonet in the inventory of November 1862; another member calls it "the old Vincennes musket with saber bayonet" (p. 233)

items.printed: breech-loading rifles
items.note: the pattern is not named in the passage

items.printed: the rifle of the regiment, caliber "may be reckoned as .69" (882 of them, forty-seven unserviceable)
items.note: the Vincennes rifle named in the sentence before the quotation (the OCR prints "Yiiicennes rifle, caliber .09"); also "our Vincennes rifles were of .69 caliber, the same as the old Harper's Ferry musket" (p. 75)

items.printed: a full supply of new .58 caliber Springfield rifles
items.note: no model year named; Beaver: "the Regiment is supplied with the best arms in the world"

items.printed: the lighter .58 caliber Springfield rifles
items.note: a recollection of Company I; the exchange is dated "about the middle of April" here and before 9 February in Beaver's account (line above)

items.printed: .58 caliber Springfield rifles
items.note: inferred for 2 July 1863; the Spencer repeating rifle came to the regiment in October 1864

items.printed: the Second Corps trefoil in red, the colour of the First Division
items.note: no passage read states this regiment's badge; the regiment belonged to the First Division (organization table, lines 0023-0063) and the division's colour is red

items.printed: overcoats and dress coats packed and sent to Washington for storage
items.note: about the middle of April 1863; a Company I account

items.printed: the light shelter tent
items.note: in place of the A tents, about the middle of April 1863

p. 301 and the chapter on Gettysburg: the strength of the corps ("fewer than ten thousand") and the losses of the divisions and brigades; no strength of a brigade

gaps.note: No figure for the strength of these units at Gettysburg was found in the reports (Mallon R113; the 1st Company Massachusetts Sharpshooters made no report; Coons R117; Lockwood R122; Dent R125, Smyth R123; Haskell R131), Fox, the state volumes or the regimental histories on disk. Colonel Devereux writes that his regiment and the 42d New York together "numbered but 290 men" when sent to Humphreys on 2 July (OR27-1-R110 p. 443): a figure for two regiments, not divided here. Ford says the 1st Company Massachusetts Sharpshooters had 233 officers and men on its rolls in all (a roll of the war, not a strength at Gettysburg).

searched.terms: R098, R099, R104, R109, R115, R116, R123, R128 (the division and brigade reports) and the reports of the regiments R100-R114, R117-R131, whole text, regex: (\d[\d,]*|\d{3})\s*(men|muskets|rifles|strong|effective|present|officers) and (numbered|strength|went into|took into|carried into|entered|present for duty)
p. 301 and the chapter on Gettysburg: the strength of the corps ("fewer than ten thousand") and the losses of the divisions and brigades; no strength of a brigade

the entries of the regiments of the brigades: the Gettysburg sentences (losses; "engaged" only for the 19th Maine, 15th and 19th Massachusetts, 1st Minnesota, 7th Michigan, 82d New York, 71st Pennsylvania, 111th New York)
section NY1-S077 (42d New York) and the sections of the 125th New York; regex of the first entry
the history of the 14th Indiana (offset 135283 onward): enrollment and losses of the war, none for Gettysburg
the account of the Twelfth: the strength on 30 June and 13 July (used in the lines), the other regiments of Smyth's brigade have no figure
the passages on the sharpshooter companies attached to the 1st Minnesota

gaps.note: No figure for the strength of these units at Gettysburg was found in the reports (Mallon R113; the 1st Company Massachusetts Sharpshooters made no report; Coons R117; Lockwood R122; Dent R125, Smyth R123; Haskell R131), Fox, the state volumes or the regimental histories on disk. Colonel Devereux writes that his regiment and the 42d New York together "numbered but 290 men" when sent to Humphreys on 2 July (OR27-1-R110 p. 443): a figure for two regiments, not divided here. Ford says the 1st Company Massachusetts Sharpshooters had 233 officers and men on its rolls in all (a roll of the war, not a strength at Gettysburg).

gaps.note: Successions of command that no source read states: who commanded the 108th New York while its lieutenant colonel (Pierce) held the Second Brigade on 3 July; who held the 14th Connecticut when Morris, its colonel, took the brigade by 5 July (Major Ellis signs on 6 July); who commanded the 39th New York after Major Hildebrandt was wounded on 3 July; whether anyone took the 7th West Virginia from Lieut. gaps.note: No figure for the strength of these units at Gettysburg was found in the reports (Mallon R113; the 1st Company Massachusetts Sharpshooters made no report; Coons R117; Lockwood R122; Dent R125, Smyth R123; Haskell R131), Fox, the state volumes or the regimental histories on disk. Colonel Devereux writes that his regiment and the 42d New York together "numbered but 290 men" when sent to Humphreys on 2 July (OR27-1-R110 p. 443): a figure for two regiments, not divided here. Ford says the 1st Company Massachusetts Sharpshooters had 233 officers and men on its rolls in all (a roll of the war, not a strength at Gettysburg).

gaps.note: Successions of command that no source read states: who commanded the 108th New York while its lieutenant colonel (Pierce) held the Second Brigade on 3 July; who held the 14th Connecticut when Morris, its colonel, took the brigade by 5 July (Major Ellis signs on 6 July); who commanded the 39th New York after Major Hildebrandt was wounded on 3 July; whether anyone took the 7th West Virginia from Lieut. change.detail: took command when Harris was relieved; wounded about dark and retired at 11 p.m.

change.detail: commanded the regiment from 11 p.m. on 2 July; fell in the countercharge with a captured flag in his hand (Dent: "mortally wounded")

change.detail: the command devolved on him when Smith fell; he signs the report

gaps.note: Successions of command that no source read states: who commanded the 108th New York while its lieutenant colonel (Pierce) held the Second Brigade on 3 July; who held the 14th Connecticut when Morris, its colonel, took the brigade by 5 July (Major Ellis signs on 6 July); who commanded the 39th New York after Major Hildebrandt was wounded on 3 July; whether anyone took the 7th West Virginia from Lieut. Col. Lockwood (wounded; he signs the report); who commanded the 126th New York once Lieut. Col. Bull held the brigade; who commanded the First Brigade after Harrow took the division on 3 July and when (the table names Colonel Heath second); and who commanded the Second Division from the battle of 2 July until 1 p.m. on 3 July while Gibbon had the corps (his report: "again during the battle of the 2d"; Harrow signs as commanding the division, the reports do not date it).

designations: Third Brigade, Third Division, Second Army Corps

commanders.name: George L. Willard
commanders.role: colonel of the 125th New York commanding the brigade

change.detail: killed by a shot from a rebel battery as the brigade re-formed after its charge on the evening of the 2d

commanders.name: Eliakim Sherrill
commanders.role: colonel of the 126th New York; commanded the brigade after Willard fell

change.detail: assumed command after Willard fell on the evening of the 2d; killed about 4 p.m. on the 3d

commanders.name: James M. Bull
commanders.role: lieutenant colonel of the 126th New York; commanded the brigade after Sherrill

change.detail: the command of the brigade devolved on him when Sherrill fell; he signs the report of 8 July as commanding the brigade

the Gettysburg chapter, "Morris", "Ellis": Morris at the head of the brigade by 5 July; no commander named for the 14th Connecticut other than Major Ellis

gaps.note: Successions of command that no source read states: who commanded the 108th New York while its lieutenant colonel (Pierce) held the Second Brigade on 3 July; who held the 14th Connecticut when Morris, its colonel, took the brigade by 5 July (Major Ellis signs on 6 July); who commanded the 39th New York after Major Hildebrandt was wounded on 3 July; whether anyone took the 7th West Virginia from Lieut. Col. Lockwood (wounded; he signs the report); who commanded the 126th New York once Lieut. Col. Bull held the brigade; who commanded the First Brigade after Harrow took the division on 3 July and when (the table names Colonel Heath second); and who commanded the Second Division from the battle of 2 July until 1 p.m. on 3 July while Gibbon had the corps (his report: "again during the battle of the 2d"; Harrow signs as commanding the division, the reports do not date it).

gaps.note: No brigade figure in the record: the abstracts and returns of pp. 151-155 stop at the division and the corps (and the artillery brigade); General Graham was wounded and taken, and Tippin's and Madill's reports give no brigade strength. Craft (1885) p. 114 says only that "Graham's entire brigade did not have the strength of two full regiments". Adding the regiment figures of this file on their mixed bases gives about 1,780 (57th 209, 63d 295 for duty, 68th 320, 105th 284, 114th 463 present, 141st 209): a sum, not a documented brigade figure, and not entered.

commanders.name: Hiram Berdan
commanders.role: colonel; also commanded both sharpshooter regiments and then the Second Brigade

commanders.name: Casper Trepp
commanders.role: lieutenant colonel; signs the regiment's report as commanding

casualty_return|1863-07-01/1863-07-04.basis: a row of the Return of Casualties; 1863-07-01/1863-07-04; as of 1863-07-01/1863-07-04; 1 line (OR27-1-R013)

value.note: per man, "not more than about 5 rounds"; the detachment that Lieutenant-Colonel Trepp took out for the second reconnaissance, counted after its return and before it went to support Captain Baker's line

value.detail: 2 July, about 7.30 a. m.: a detachment of 100 sharpshooters sent forward to discover what the enemy was doing; Berdan posted it on the crest beyond the Emmitsburg road, where it fired nearly all day until driven in about 5 p. m., its ammunition spent

value.attached: the Third Maine Regiment, in support, on the second reconnaissance
value.detail: 2 July, about 11 a. m.: another detachment of 100 sharpshooters, with the Third Maine as support, sent farther to the left to feel the enemy (the Pitzer's Run fight); Trepp names the companies: D and E on the left, F and I on the right

value.attached: the Fifth Army Corps (to protect batteries), under Captain J. H. Baker
value.detail: 3 July: Captain J. H. Baker detached with Companies C, I and K; they protected batteries; Corporal Wellington Fitch of Company C captured a squad of rebel sharpshooters

value.attached: covering the front of the Sixth Corps, under Captain Baker
value.detail: 3 July: a detachment of about 100 sharpshooters under Captain Baker, as sharpshooters, to cover the front of the Sixth Corps; they stayed all day, advanced toward night and captured 18 prisoners

items.printed: the angular bayonet
items.note: the book contrasts it with the sabre bayonet of a privately owned Sharps rifle (p. 36) and says the men preferred the angular bayonet as less cumbersome; the catalogue's socket bayonet is the triangular-bladed one

items.printed: Colt's five-shot revolving rifles
items.note: the catalogue has no Colt revolving rifle (a placeholder "revolving_and_other_breechloaders_gap" only)

items.printed: target rifles of different descriptions (two companies, C of Michigan and E of New Hampshire; the Vermont company a few guns)
items.note: the book says "fully armed" with target rifles of different descriptions

items.printed: the long expected Sharps rifles (linen or skin cartridges, 52 caliber, with primers)
items.note: The passage names "Sharps" rifles of 52 caliber and does not name the year of the pattern; the catalogue has one Sharps rifle, the .52 of 1859, and the mapping to it is the catalogue's, not the source's.

items.printed: the Sharps rifles
items.note: the book names "Sharps rifles" and not the year of the pattern; the mapping to the catalogue's one Sharps rifle is the catalogue's

items.printed: Sharp's rifles of an improved pattern and excellent finish, manufactured expressly for their use
items.note: the book says "Sharp's rifles of an improved pattern"; no year or calibre; the catalogue has one Sharps rifle, the .52 of 1859, and the mapping to it is the catalogue's

items.printed: knapsack of hair-covered calfskin, with cooking kit attached
the hair-covered knapsacks, the last of them lost at Gaines' Mill
items.note: the detachment of Companies C and G lost its knapsacks when they were unslung for the closing charge; the book calls them "the last of the hair-covered knapsacks"; it does not say what the men carried afterward

items.printed: gray felt, seamless overcoats (abandoned)
items.note: good rain shedders but stiff as a board when wet; abandoned; the catalogue has no such overcoat

items.printed: a large amount of green clothing, with overcoats (which were the regulation blue) and blankets formerly turned in, received and distributed
items.note: at the camp near Culpeper on 17 September 1863; the book does not say when the clothing, overcoats and blankets had been turned in

items.printed: the "Kearny patch", the title to wear which the regiment had earned
items.note: the red diamond patch of the division

items.printed: dark green coat
items.note: the passage says "coat"; the catalogue's one Berdan green coat is the frock coat

items.printed: the Green Coats ("There goes them Sharp fellows")
items.note: the book speaks of the Sharpshooters of the march of 1 May 1863; "Green Coats" is its name for the men; the passage does not say that every man wore a green coat

items.printed: our green coats (interspersed with the "boys in blue")
items.note: Captain Marble speaks of Company G; the sentence closes with "It was thus we marched to the fields of Gettysburg"

items.printed: cap with black plume (dark green)
items.note: the passage says "dark green coat and cap with black plume"; "dark green cap" is the reading of the shared adjective; the catalogue's green kepi has no plume

items.printed: "Havelocks," a gray, round hat with wide, black visor
items.note: worn for a time, mostly on outpost duty or in bad weather; the catalogue has no havelock

items.printed: knapsacks well packed, haversacks and canteens filled
items.note: on the march of 1 May 1863, with "a full complement of ammunition"

items.printed: leather leggins
light blue trowsers
items.note: the catalogue's sky-blue kersey trouser is the regulation one; the passage does not name the cloth

items.printed: green trowsers (exchanged for the light blue "afterward")
items.note: the book gives no date of the exchange; no line of it says which trousers the men wore on 2 July 1863

value.attached: the Fifth Army Corps (to protect batteries), under Captain J. H. Baker
value.detail: 3 July: Captain J. H. Baker detached with Companies C, I and K; they protected batteries; Corporal Wellington Fitch of Company C captured a squad of rebel sharpshooters

value.attached: covering the front of the Sixth Corps, under Captain Baker
value.detail: 3 July: a detachment of about 100 sharpshooters under Captain Baker, as sharpshooters, to cover the front of the Sixth Corps; they stayed all day, advanced toward night and captured 18 prisoners
